message.content:
**Traffic Laws in Texas – A Quick Reference Guide** | Topic | Key Points | Where to Find More Info | |-------|------------|------------------------| | **Speed Limits** | • Posted limits are the law.
• 55 mph on rural interstates, 65 mph on urban interstates, 45 mph on highways with 2–3 lanes each direction, 35 mph on 4‑lane highways, 25 mph on 5‑lane highways.
• “No‑limit” roads (e.g., I‑10, I‑20) have no posted speed limit but drivers must drive “reasonably and safely.” | Texas Transportation Code §545.001 | | **Seat‑Belt & Child Restraint** | • All occupants must wear seat belts.
• Children under 8 must be in a child safety seat or booster.
• The “no‑seat‑belt” law applies to all vehicles. | Texas Transportation Code §545.002 | | **DUI / Alcohol** | • Blood alcohol concentration (BAC) of 0.08% or higher is illegal.
• Zero‑tolerance for drivers under 21 (BAC ≥ 0.02%).
• Penalties include fines, license suspension, mandatory alcohol‑education programs, and possible jail time. | Texas Transportation Code §§545.021–545.023 | | **Texting & Phone Use** | • Hand‑held phone use while driving is prohibited.
• “Hands‑free” devices are allowed.
• Texting while driving is a moving‑violation offense. | Texas Transportation Code §545.025 | | **Right‑of‑Way** | • Stop at red lights, stop signs, and yield signs.
• Yield to pedestrians in crosswalks.
• “Right‑of‑way” rules apply at intersections without signals. | Texas Transportation Code §545.030 | | **Lane Discipline** | • Keep to the right lane unless passing.
• Use turn lanes when turning left or right.
• “Lane‑change” violations can result in fines. | Texas Transportation Code §545.040 | | **School Bus Rules** | • Stop for school buses with flashing red lights and extended stop sign.
• Do not pass a stopped school bus until the lights are off and the stop sign is retracted. | Texas Transportation Code §545.050 | | **Parking Regulations** | • No parking in front of fire hydrants, in front of driveways, or in designated no‑parking zones.
• Parking in a handicap space requires a valid permit. | Texas Transportation Code §545.060 | | **Vehicle Equipment** | • Must have working headlights, taillights, brake lights, turn signals, and horn.
• Tires must have adequate tread depth (minimum 2 / 32 in). | Texas Transportation Code §545.070 | | **Insurance Requirements** | • Minimum liability coverage: $30,000 for bodily injury per person, $60,000 for total bodily injury per accident, $25,000 for property damage. | Texas Insurance Code §151.001 | | **Special Vehicle Rules** | • Bicyclists must ride in the lane if one exists; otherwise, they may ride on the shoulder.
• Motorcycles must use the same lane as other vehicles. | Texas Transportation Code §545.080 | | **Penalties & Enforcement** | • Moving‑violation fines range from $50 to $500.
• Repeat offenders face higher fines and license suspensions.
• Courts may impose community service or mandatory education courses. | Texas Transportation Code §545.090 | --- ### How to Stay Updated 1. **Texas Department of Transportation (TxDOT)** – Official website: [https://www.txdot.gov](https://www.txdot.gov) *TxDOT publishes updates on road conditions, construction, and traffic regulations.* 2. **Texas Transportation Code** – Accessible online via the Texas Legislature’s website: [https://statutes.capitol.texas.gov](https://statutes.capitol.texas.gov) *Search for “Transportation Code” and navigate to Chapter 545 for traffic laws.* 3. **Texas Department of Public Safety (DPS)** – Driver licensing and enforcement: [https://www.dps.texas.gov](https://www.dps.texas.gov) *Provides information on DUI laws, license suspensions, and driver education.* 4. **Local County Courts** – For specific case law or recent rulings, check the county court’s website or contact the clerk’s office. --- ### Quick Tips for Safe Driving in Texas - **Always keep your seat belt fastened** – it’s a legal requirement and saves lives. - **Avoid distractions** – put your phone away or use a hands‑free system. - **Know your speed limits** – they’re posted on signs; obey them. - **Respect school buses** – stop and wait until it’s safe to proceed. - **Check your insurance** – ensure you meet the minimum liability coverage. Feel free to let me know if you need deeper details on any specific section, such as DUI penalties, school bus regulations, or how to file a traffic ticket appeal!
